note: Entries the enricher validator rejects that a re-run does not clear. Recorded rather than hand-fixed, per the run rules. Not halting: the run rate is far under the 10% line.

lexicon_defect.what: derived-bulk.jsonl is missing real irregular inflections and carries bogus regular ones in their place

cases.do: has did/done/doing/dos/doed but NOT 'does' - while go->goes and have->has are both present

lexicon_defect.impact: two-fold. (1) enrich_validate's example_mentions rejects correct examples that use the real plural or third-person form. (2) the shipped Resolver cannot take a reader from 'women', 'gentlemen' or 'does' to its headword - a stage 6 search bug on three very common forms.
lexicon_defect.not_fixed_here: regenerating the lexicon mid-run would move the ruler this run is measured against. It belongs with steps 9-13, where derived-bulk is rebuilt anyway.

rubric_collision.what: the learner line must be 3-45 words and must not equal the gloss. Some glosses are two words, so a faithful rewrite is either 2 words or the gloss itself.
rubric_collision.survived: each of these was re-run once and came back with the same fault, which is the signal that it is the rubric and not the batch.
rubric_collision.not_fixed_here: changing enricher.md makes the next run a new baseline rather than a comparison. It is Shawn's call.
rubric_collision.pattern: 9 of the 12 blocked entries fail this way, and every one has a two- or three-word gloss (happen; almost not; seldom; two times; the introduction of something new). A faithful rewrite of a two-word gloss is either the gloss itself or under the 3-word floor, so enricher.md section 1 asks for two things that cannot both hold there. This is a rubric problem, not a batch problem: re-running does not clear it, and it recurred identically across two runs of the same packets.
